# Reference Case C — AI-generated code approaching production

**Codokey Reference Cases v1.0.0 · validator `tools/codokey-check.mjs`**

> A review requirement is only meaningful if the approver is independent of the agent and of the person who asked for the change, if approval applies to the final revision, and if deployment is a separate human decision.

## Scenario

An agent opens a pull request that changes application code and a deployment workflow. The case evaluates two policies (governed and ungoverned) and two histories of the same kind of change (independent approval vs. requester self-approval with a stale owner approval and an AI review-assistant approval).

## Assumptions

- Identities prefixed app: or bot: are non-human and never count as approvers.
- An approval counts only if it is on headRevision.
- Policy settings are modeled on GitHub branch protection and environments; GitLab protected branches and deployment approvals provide equivalents.

## Synthetic inputs

- policy.governed.json / policy.ungoverned.json — branch protection and production environment settings
- change.independent-approval.json — approval from a code owner on the latest revision; deployment approved by a reviewer other than the trigger
- change.self-approved.json — only the requester, an AI reviewer, and a stale approval

All values are synthetic. No real credentials, repositories, or systems are used.

## Protocol layers

04 Review Boundary, 05 Deployment Control, 01 Code Origin

## Control expectations

- Required approval excludes agent and requester and applies to the latest push (CK-RB-01).
- Protection binds administrators (CK-RB-04).
- Sensitive paths need code-owner review (CK-RB-02).
- Production deployment requires an independent human reviewer; agents are not deployers (CK-DC-01, FZ-3).
- Production secrets are scoped to the protected environment (CK-DC-02).

## Observable pass/fail conditions

| Check | Condition |
|---|---|
| C1–C3, C5–C6 | Policy checks: evaluate the settings themselves. |
| C4 | Change check: at least the required number of qualifying approvals on the head revision, including the required code owner. |
| C7 | Change check: a qualifying deployment approval exists when a deployment was triggered. |

## Evidence requirements (real-world equivalent)

Exported branch-protection or ruleset configuration, CODEOWNERS, environment protection settings, and the pull-request review and deployment-approval history.

## Reproduce

```sh
node tools/codokey-check.mjs production-path --change cases/c-production-path/change.independent-approval.json --policy cases/c-production-path/policy.governed.json   # expect PASS
node tools/codokey-check.mjs production-path --change cases/c-production-path/change.self-approved.json --policy cases/c-production-path/policy.governed.json   # expect FAIL (C4, C7)
node tools/codokey-check.mjs production-path --change cases/c-production-path/change.independent-approval.json --policy cases/c-production-path/policy.ungoverned.json   # expect FAIL (C1, C2, C3, C5, C6, C7)
```

## Expected outcome

governed + independent → PASS (merge and deploy allowed). governed + self-approved → FAIL on C4, C7. ungoverned + independent → FAIL on C1, C2, C3, C5, C6, C7 even though one independent approval happened to exist.

## Limitations

- Models a single protected branch and environment.
- Does not evaluate review quality — only who approved what.
- Platform features vary by plan; see evidence register limitations.
